title: Evacuate Scaleback and Backfill Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft for the end-to-end procedure used when we need to evacuate node(s) or entire racks due to failing accelerators, degraded NICs, or urgent hardware maintenance and to safely scale back traffic and backfill capacity without violating latency SLOs. It covers: triage, cordon/drain patterns, prioritized workload evacuation (priority queues), graceful degrade toggles, verifying KV/prefix cache persistence, safe GPU replacement checklist, and warm-up/backfill orchestration.

Intended audience:
- Oncall SREs (primary)
- Infra engineers performing physical GPU swaps (secondary)
- Platform/serving owners responsible for rollout and performance targets

Quick goals (operational):
1) Protect user-facing latency SLOs during hardware replacement or sudden capacity loss.
2) Minimize failed or timed-out inferences by orderly evacuation and prioritized routing.
3) Bring replacement capacity online and fully warm before shifting production traffic.
4) Capture decisions + artifacts for post-incident review.

Pre-incident preparation (must be validated quarterly):
- Playbook owner: eng-sre (Aisha) reviews quarterly.
- Validate GPU replacement kit and spare node images present in rack-level inventory.
- Confirm autoscaler policies: cluster-autoscaler (enabled) has warmup hooks configured.
- Ensure priority classes are defined for critical-serving (p0-serving), batch, and low-priority (idle-evals).
- Backfill script location: github:infra/ops-scripts (ops/backfill.sh) — ensure latest token and SSH key access.
- Slack channel: #sre-ops, Pager rotation list up-to-date.
- Health dashboards: infra/gpu-health, infra/latency-by-model, routing/queue-depth.

Triage (first 10 minutes):
1) Gather facts (commands and metrics):
   - Which node(s) affected? `kubectl get nodes -l accelerator=... -o wide`
   - GPU health: `nvidia-smi -q` (if reachable) or node exporter metrics.
   - Symptoms: kernel oops, ECC errors, high PCIe errors, pod restarts, OOMs, NVLINK fail, degraded NVSwitch.
   - Top impact: which models/tenants running on affected node? `kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>`
   - Current cluster utilization: percent GPU and CPU allocated, queue depth for p0-serving.
2) If symptoms are severe (memory corruption, repeated machine reboots, or smoke): page hardware-oncall and set severity to Sev2/Sev1 as needed.
3) Notify stakeholders: post to #sre-ops with short TL;DR, affected node, impact, early mitigation intent.

Decision: live repair vs. evacuate-and-replace
- If node is reachable and transient (e.g., driver panic recoverable) and servicing stateful caches intact, try a non-disruptive driver restart or cordon-probe.
- If repeated reboots, persistent ECC errors, or hardware error counters rising -> proceed to evacuate and replace. Document decision and who signed off.

Evacuation plan (cordon & prioritized drain):
1) Set cordon: `kubectl cordon <node>` — prevents new pods scheduling.
2) Apply PDB-aware drain for high-priority pods first: we use priority class ordering to minimize p0-serving disruption.
   - Step drain command: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='!priorityClass=low' --timeout=15m` (adjust timeout based on model cold-start profile).
3) Use eviction-safety for p0-serving: temporarily increase replica counts for p0 deployments (if capacity exists) or trigger router-level soft-fallback to warm standby region.
4) For batch/low-priority pods, allow immediate preemption or eviction (set TTL to 2m) so that critical pods can run elsewhere.
5) Monitor replication and routing: watch for queue length spikes and tail latency — if tail exceeds threshold, pause further drains and push fallback routing.

Graceful degrade toggles (when evacuation reduces capacity below known thresholds):
- If available GPU capacity < 20% of p0 demand (calc in dashboard), flip degrade flags:
  - Reduce temperature sampling frequency (model-specific).
  - Enable aggressive token-capping in routing (max-tokens-per-request lowered).
  - Switch non-critical workloads to cached-responses or shorter context.
- How to flip: call `infra-toggle degrade-mode on` (ops script) OR update ConfigMap `routing/quality-controls` with key `degrade-mode: true`. Post to Slack when toggled.

Replacement / physical GPU swap checklist (for infra engineer):
- Safety: power down node following rack SOP, label cables, ESD precautions.
- Log required: chassis id, serial numbers of old and new GPU, firmware versions.
- Swap: insert replacement, ensure correct power connector seating (12V aux), verify physical NVLink bridging if present.
- First boot: watch BMC and IPMI logs, confirm BIOS recognizes card.
- Driver validation: `nvidia-smi` shows expected device and memory.
- NIC and PCIe link checks.
- Mark as replacement completed in incident ticket.

Backfill and warmup orchestration (automated + manual steps):
1) Add node back to cluster by removing maintenance tag and uncordoning: `kubectl uncordon <node>` only after warmup passed.
2) Warmup sequence (must complete before directing traffic):
   - Pull model artifacts/cache prefetch: run warmup job `infra/warmup-job --node <node> --models <critical-models>` that does a constrained set of inference passes to populate KV/prefix caches and kernel JITs.
   - Run N warmup requests (default N=40 per model) and confirm latencies within 1.2x baseline.
   - Confirm GPU memory footprint stabilizes and no OOMs during warmup.
3) Health checks: ensure node exporter, nvidia-smi, and runtime agent report healthy for 10m.
4) Gradually reintroduce traffic by updating router weight: shift 5-10% of p0-serving at a time for 5-minute windows while observing tail latency and error-rate.

Autoscaler & capacity injections notes:
- If autoscaler fails to spin up replacements due to quota, use manual backfill script `ops/backfill.sh --region <r> --count <n>` to provision on-demand nodes with correct instance types.
- For preemptible instances, consider reserved spare pool for critical-serving to avoid preemption-induced variability.
- Document any manual quota increases and ticket them to cloud-ops.

Observability and metrics to watch during the incident:
- infra/gpu-utilization (per-node and cluster), infra/gpu-error-count, infra/latency-p50/p95/p99 by model, routing/queue-depth p0/p1, autoscaler/scale-events, pod/eviction-rate, k8s/pod-scheduled-latency.
- Alert thresholds: p99 latency > 2x baseline for more than 3 min -> trigger rollback of traffic shift.

Communication play (timeline):
- 0–10m: triage and announcement (SRE oncall posts initial message).
- 10–30m: decision and action (evacuate or live repair).
- 30–90m: physical swap or recovery attempt; update Slack every 20m.
- 90–180m: warmup and traffic reintroduction.
- Post-incident: internal summary + RCA within 48 hours.

Runbook testing (quarterly):
- Tests to run against staging clusters:
  - Simulated GPU fail by cordon+taint and verify warmup job returns expected latencies.
  - Validate degrade-mode toggles and ensure routers respect config map changes.
  - End-to-end: physical replacement simulation using spare node image restore.

Post-incident checklist / retrospective notes (template to fill):
1) Timeline of events (UTC).
2) Root cause - hardware vs software vs human error.
3) What worked well? (e.g., warmup job prevented service outage).
4) What broke? (e.g., autoscaler quota prevented replacement).
5) Action items (owner + due date).
6) Test or validation required before marking action closed.

Open questions / TODO (working list):
- How to stage KV cache sync between nodes quickly without violating cache consistency? (Ravi to prototype delta-sync approach)
- Evaluate whether warmup N=40 is adequate for larger models (>70B). Need perf tests (Julian).
- Decide on a default spare pool size for p0-serving capacity (proposal due EOW).

Incident notes (example excerpt from a recent drill):
- 2026-01-20 03:12 UTC: Detected rising ECC errors on node infra-gpu-17 (driver timeouts).
- 03:18: cordon + drain applied; prioritized p0-serving moved off within 9 minutes.
- 03:40: node rebooted but failed driver init; hardware-oncall scheduled swap.
- 04:25: Replacement GPU installed; warmup job executed (25 requests/model). p99 latency spiked x1.6 during first 2 minutes then stabilized to x1.1.
- Post-mortem: recommended increase warmup job to N=50 for 70B models; created JIRA-INC-4392.

Appendix (useful commands & scripts):
- `kubectl cordon <node>`
- `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
- Warmup job: `infra/warmup-job --node <node> --models small-embed,chat-small`
- Backfill: `ops/backfill.sh --count 3 --type p4d --region us-west1`
- Toggle degrade: `infra-toggle degrade-mode on`

Notes to self:
- Keep the playbook light and actionable; avoid too many branching paths in oncall.
- Add a short checklist card in the SRE pager rotation so oncall can follow with minimal context.

File history: draft started 2025-11-02, iterated after Jan 2026 warmup drill.

If you review this doc, please: add comments inline, tag the owner, and link any additional runbooks that overlap (e.g., node-decommission, autoscaler-ops).
